rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening statement may be reported as part of the preceding prayer or begin a new sentence.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا يكلف الله نفسا ﴾ محكى عنهم أو مستأنف

rows.speaker: شرح التأويلات
rows.claim: Obligation is limited to acts a person can perform, since responsibility concerns deeds within one’s ability.
rows.anchor: إلا طاقتها وقدرتها لأن التكليف لا يرد إلا بفعل يقدر عليه المكلف

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Capacity is what one can bear without constraint or embarrassment, short of the utmost exertion; people could pray, fast, or make pilgrimage more than required.
rows.anchor: الوسع ما يسع الإنسان ولا يضيق عليه ولا يحرج فيه

words: لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good is called kasb and evil iktisab because the iftiʿāl form suggests recoil: the soul recoils from evil and exerts itself for good.
rows.anchor: وخص الخير بالكسب والشر بالاكتساب لأن الافتعال للانكماش

words: لا تؤاخذنا إن نسينا أو أخطأنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer implies that God could hold people accountable for forgetfulness or error, contrary to the Muʿtazila, since these can be avoided in some measure; otherwise the request is pointless.
rows.anchor: ودل هذا على جواز المؤاخذة فى النسيان والخطأ خلافا للمعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isr is a heavy load that pins its bearer in place; metaphorically it denotes hard obligations such as killing oneself or cutting impurity from skin or clothing.
rows.anchor: عبأ يأصر حامله أى يحبسه مكانه لثقله استعير للتكليف الشاق

words: كما حملته على الذين من قبلنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people burdened with such earlier obligations are the Jews.
rows.anchor: استعير للتكليف الشاق من نحو قتل الأنفس وقطع موضع النجاسة من الجلد والثوب وغير ذلك

words: ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This request concerns protection from punishments that befell earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: من العقوبات النازلة بمن قبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requests are not redundant: pardon erases major sins, while forgiveness covers minor sins.
rows.anchor: وليس بتكرار فالأول للكبائر والثاني للصغائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative gloss assigns pardon, forgiveness, and mercy protection respectively from metamorphosis, being swallowed by the earth, and drowning.
rows.anchor: الأول من المسخ والثاني من الخسف والثالث من الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy may mean making the scales of our deeds heavy despite our having no good deeds to offer.
rows.anchor: بتثقيل ميزاننا مع افلاسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā can mean our master, helper, or the one who manages our affairs.
rows.anchor: سيدنا ونحن عبيدك أو ناصرنا أو متولى أمورنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for victory follows because a master is expected to aid his servants.
rows.anchor: فمن حق المولى أن ينصر عبيده فى الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says reciting the closing verses beginning «Āmana al-rasūl» at night suffices the reciter.
rows.anchor: من قرأ آمن الرسول إلى آخره فى ليلة كفتاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says reciting those two verses after the final night prayer substitutes for night vigil.
rows.anchor: من قرأهما بعد العشاء الآخرة أجزأتاه عن قيام الليل

rows.speaker: على
rows.claim: ʿAlī is cited as saying that the closing verses of al-Baqara are a treasure from beneath the Throne.
rows.anchor: لما روى عن على رضى الله عنه خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some disapproved of saying «I read al-Baqara» and preferred «I read the sūra in which al-Baqara is mentioned».
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم يكره ذلك بل يقال قرأت السورة التى تذكر فيها البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat Āl ʿImrān was revealed in Medina and has two hundred verses.
rows.anchor: سورة آل عمران نزلت بالمدينة وهى مائتا آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adverb «idh» is governed by «qālat» or by an omitted imperative «remember».
rows.anchor: وإذ منصوب به أو باضمار اذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of ʿImrān ibn Māthān, Mary’s mother and Jesus’s grandmother, was Ḥanna daughter of Fāqūdhā.
rows.anchor: هى امرأة عمران بن ماثان أم مريم جدة عيسى وهى حنة بنت فاقوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Nadhartu» means she made something binding upon herself.
rows.anchor: أوجبت ﴿ ما في بطني محررا ﴾ هو حال من ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She vowed the child in her womb as freed for service at the Jerusalem sanctuary, beyond her control and not for her use; this vow was lawful then.
rows.anchor: بمعنى الذى أى معتقا لخدمة بيت المقدس لا يد لى عليه ولا أستخدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes «muḥarrar» as devoted purely to worship, like «ḥurr» for pure clay.
rows.anchor: أو مخلصا للعبادة يقال طين حر أى خالص

rows.speaker: مدنى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Medinan reader and Abū ʿAmr read «fa-taqabbal minnī»; taqabbul is acceptance with approval.
rows.anchor: فتقبل مني ﴾ مدنى و أبو عمرو والتقبل أخذ الشئ على الرضا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Mary and approved her in the vow in place of a male child.
rows.anchor: قبل الله مريم ورضى بها فى النذر مكان الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabūl can name the means of acceptance; here it is God’s special favor in assigning Mary the place of a boy, unprecedented for a girl.
rows.anchor: قيل القبول اسم ما يقبل به الشئ كالسعوط بما يسعط به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, her acceptance was her mother’s handing her over immediately after birth, before she could grow old enough for sanctuary service.
rows.anchor: أو بأن تسلمها من أمها عقيب الولادة قبل أن تنشأ وتصلح للسدانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Ḥanna wrapped newborn Mary and brought her to the temple priests descended from Aaron; they competed to care for her because she was the imam’s daughter and the Banū Māthān were Israelite leaders.
rows.anchor: روى أن حنة لما ولدت مريم لفتها فى خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account, Zechariah claimed precedence through kinship; after twenty-seven men cast their pens in a river, his rose above the water while the others sank, so he became her guardian.
rows.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا فوق الماء ورسبت أقلامهم فتكفلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing treats qabūl as a verbal noun with an omitted genitive: acceptance by one possessing excellent acceptance, namely God’s special favor.
rows.anchor: فتقبلها بذى قبول حسن أى بمر ذى قبول حسن وهو الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Growing her with good growth is a metaphor for her good upbringing.
rows.anchor: مجاز عن التربية الحسنة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the best growth is that whose fruit was Jesus.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء ما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Nabātan» is either an unconventional verbal noun or an underlying «she grew a growth».
rows.anchor: ونباتا مصدر على خلاف الصدر أو التقدير فنبتت نباتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Kaffalahā» means either that God accepted her or undertook her care.
rows.anchor: قبلها أو ضمن القيام بأمرها

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read the verb with doubled fāʾ, making God the subject who appoints Zechariah as guardian; the other form says Zechariah cared for her.
rows.anchor: وكفلها كوفى أى كفلها الله زكريا يعنى جعله كافلاها

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: The Kufans except Abū Bakr read Zakariyyā shortened throughout the Qurʾān; Abū Bakr lengthens it and reads it in the accusative here, while others lengthen it in the nominative as at later occurrences.
rows.anchor: بالقصر كوفى غير أبى بكر فى كل القرآن وقرأ أبو بكر بالمد والنصب هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Zakariyyā means in Hebrew one who constantly remembers and glorifies God.
rows.anchor: ومعناه فى العبرى دائم الذكر والتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miḥrāb may be a chamber Zechariah built for her in the mosque, a raised room reached by stairs; it may instead mean the finest, foremost seat, or the name for their mosques.
rows.anchor: قيل بنى لها زكريا محرابا فى السمجد أى غرفة تصعد اليها بسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the account that Mary was secluded in the sanctuary, only Zechariah entered to see her.
rows.anchor: وكان لا يدخل عليها إلا هو وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her provision descended from Paradise; she was never nursed, and Zechariah found winter fruit with her in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: كان رزقها ينزل عليها من الجنة ولم ترضع ثديا قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah asks where she obtained this provision, which did not resemble worldly food and arrived out of season.
rows.anchor: من أين لك هذا الرزق الذى لا يشبه أرزاق الدنيا وهو آت فى غير حينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that Mary spoke while still a small child, just as Jesus spoke in the cradle.
rows.anchor: قيل تكلمت وهى صغيرة كما تكلم عيسى وهو فى المهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence «God provides for whom He wills» may continue Mary’s speech or be God’s own words.
rows.anchor: من جملة كلام مريم أو من كلام رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Without reckoning» can mean provision too abundant to measure, or a gift bestowed without accounting for or recompensing deeds.
rows.anchor: بغير تقدير لكثرته أو تفضلا بغير محاسبة ومجازاة على عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «That» points to the accounts of Ḥanna, Zechariah, John, and Mary.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما سبق من قصة حنة وزكريا ويحيى ومريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These were matters of the unseen that the Prophet knew only through revelation.
rows.anchor: يعنى أن ذلك من الغيوب التى لم تعرفها إلا بالوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pens may be divination arrows cast into the river to draw lots, or the pens used to write the Torah, chosen for the lot as a blessing.
rows.anchor: أزلامهم وهى قداحهم التى طرحوها فى النهر مقترعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause depends on an omitted phrase: they cast the pens to see who would care for her, to learn the result, or as a spoken question.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون كأنه قيل يلقونها ينظرون أيهم يكفل مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispute was a competition over who would be Mary’s guardian.
rows.anchor: فى شأنها تنافسا فى التكفل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative rejection follows fāʾ between clauses: «those are the transgressors, so do they seek another religion?»; alternatively it coordinates with an omitted «do they turn away?»
rows.anchor: دخلت همزة الانكار على الفاء العاطفة جملة على جملة والمعنى فأولئك هم الفاسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object «other than God’s religion» precedes its verb because the rejection targets the false object of worship in particular.
rows.anchor: وقدم المفعول وهو غير دين الله على فعله لأنه أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in heaven are angels; those on earth are humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: في السماوات ﴾ الملائكة ﴿ والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They submit willingly through reflection on proofs and fairness, or under compulsion by the sword, witnessing punishment, or approaching death.
rows.anchor: بالنظر فى الأدلة والإنصاف من نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Willingly and unwillingly» is adverbial, describing submission in either state.
rows.anchor: وانتصب طوعا وكرها على الحال أى طائعين ومكرهين

rows.speaker: حفص وأبو عمرو وسائر القراء
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads both verbs with yāʾ; Abū ʿAmr reads the second with tāʾ and fatḥa on its jīm; the others read both with tāʾ and that fatḥa.
rows.anchor: يبغون ويرجعون بالياء فيهما حفص وبالتاء فى الثاني وفتح الجيم أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are those seeking another religion, but all people return to God for recompense.
rows.anchor: لأن الباغين هم المتولون والراجعون جميع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God eases matters by permitting marriage to enslaved women and granting other legal dispensations.
rows.anchor: باحلال نكاح الأمة وغيره من الرخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are weak: they cannot patiently resist desires or endure the hardships of worship.
rows.anchor: لا يصبر عن الشهوات وعلى مشاق الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stole armor from his neighbor Qatāda ibn al-Nuʿmān in a flour sack; flour leaked through a hole, and Ṭuʿma hid the armor with the Jew Zayd ibn al-Samīn.
rows.anchor: روى أن طعمه بن أبيرق أحد بنى ظفر سرق درعا من جار له اسمه قتادة بن النعمان فى جراب دقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the armor was traced to the Jew, Ṭuʿma denied it under oath; the Jew said Ṭuʿma had given it to him, supported by Jewish witnesses.
rows.anchor: فقال دفعها إلى طعمة وشهد له ناس من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū Ẓafar asked the Prophet to argue for their man, fearing his disgrace and the Jew’s acquittal; the Prophet was about to do so when the verse came down.
rows.anchor: فسألوه أن يجادل عن صاحبهم وقالوا أن لم تفعل هلك صاحبنا وافتضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Bi-l-ḥaqq» means truthfully or rightly.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق ﴾ أى محقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment is according to what God made known and revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ما عرفك وأوحى به إليك

rows.speaker: أبو منصور
rows.claim: Abū Manṣūr says it means what God inspired through reasoning from revealed principles; the verse supports the permissibility of the Prophet’s ijtihād.
rows.anchor: بما ألهمك بالنظر فى أصوله المنزلة وفيه دلالة جواز الاجتهاد فى حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «For the traitors» means on their behalf: the Prophet should not litigate against the Jew for Banū Ẓafar.
rows.anchor: ولا تخاصم اليهود لأجل بنى ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor and mercy protected the Prophet and kept him from discovering the conspirators’ secret.
rows.anchor: أى عصمته ولطفه من الاطلاع على سرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group may be some of Banū Ẓafar or all of them; «them» may refer to people generally.
rows.anchor: من بنى ظفر أو المراد بالطائفة بنو ظفر والضمير فى منهم يعود إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sought to divert him from judging justly although they knew their own man was guilty.
rows.anchor: عن القضاء بالحق وتوخى طريق العدل مع علمهم بأن الجانى صاحبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attempted deception would bring harm only upon themselves.
rows.anchor: لأن وباله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could not harm the Prophet because he acted on outward facts and did not know the truth was otherwise.
rows.anchor: لأنك إنما عملت بظاهر الحال وما كان يخطر ببالك أن الحقيقة على خلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qurʾān and Wisdom is the Sunna.
rows.anchor: عليك الكتاب ﴾ القرآن ﴿ والحكمة ﴾ والسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God taught may mean religious matters and laws, or hidden matters and the secrets within hearts.
rows.anchor: من أمور الدين والشرائع أو من خفيات الأمور وضمائر القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor was great in what He taught the Prophet and bestowed upon him.
rows.anchor: فيما علمك وأنعم عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Muhammad to tell those who envy him what envy caused, so they will desist and believe his message.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى مححد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقص على حاسديه ما جرى بسبب الحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people to be told are the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: على أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sons may be Hābīl and Qābīl from Adam’s descendants, or two Israelite men.
rows.anchor: ومن صلبه هابيل وقابيل أو هما رجلان من بنى إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «In truth» may mean an account agreeing with earlier scriptures, a truthful and sound telling, or that Muhammad tells it truthfully.
rows.anchor: بالصدق موافقا لما فى كتب الأولين أو تلاوة ملتبسة بالصدق والصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «When they offered» is governed by «the account» as their story then, or is in apposition with an omitted genitive.
rows.anchor: نصب بالنبأ أى قصتهما وحديثهما فى ذلك الوقت أو بدل من النبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbān is an offering to draw near to God, whether sacrifice or charity; each brother brought his own offering.
rows.anchor: ما يتقرب به إلى الله من نسيكة أو صدقة

words: فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says God told Adam to marry each son to the other’s twin; Qābīl envied Hābīl over the more beautiful Iqlīmā, so Adam ordered offerings and fire consumed Hābīl’s.
rows.anchor: روى أنه اوحى الله تعالى إلى آدم أن يزوج كل واحد منهما توأمه الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Hābīl’s offering was accepted, Qābīl’s jealousy and anger grew and he threatened murder.
rows.anchor: فازداد قابيل حسدا وسخطا وتوعده بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hābīl means that God accepts only from the pious; Qābīl was not pious, so rejection was due to his own lack of piety, not his brother.
rows.anchor: فإنما أوتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها من لباس التقوى لا من قبلى

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh wept near death; asked why, he said he heard God say that He accepts only from the pious.
rows.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله أنه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Basaṭta» means you extended; «bāsiṭ» means one extending.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لئن بسطت ﴾ مددت ﴿ إلي يدك لتقتلني

rows.speaker: مدنى وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: The Medinan reader, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read the form «yadiya».
rows.anchor: يدي ﴾ مدنى و أبو عمرو وحفص ﴿ إليك

rows.speaker: حجازى وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Hijazis and Abū ʿAmr read the reported form «innī akhāfu».
rows.anchor: إنى أخاف حجازى و أبو عمرو

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Hābīl was stronger but scrupled to kill his brother and surrendered out of fear of God, since defense was not permitted then.
rows.anchor: قيل كان أقوى من القاتل وأبطش منه ولكن تحرج عن قتل اخيه

words: ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says refraining from defense was obligatory because it would destroy his own life and make him share the killer’s sin; Qābīl attacked treacherously while he was unaware.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل كان ذلك واجبا فإن فيه إهلاك نفسه ومشاركة للقاتل فى اثمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hābīl’s stated reason for not killing his brother is fear of God.
rows.anchor: و إنما قتله فتكا على غفلة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His soul made the murder easy and acceptable; the phrase derives from a pasture being spacious for someone.
rows.anchor: فوسعته ويسرته من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The murder took place either at ʿAqabat Ḥirāʾ or at Baṣra.
rows.anchor: فقتله ﴾ عند عقبة حراء أو بالبصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The murdered brother was twenty years old.
rows.anchor: البصرة والمقتول ابن عشرين سنة ﴿ فأصبح من الخاسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the murder, Qābīl became one of the losers.
rows.anchor: المقتول ابن عشرين سنة ﴿ فأصبح من الخاسرين

words: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding alliance with those who must be opposed, the passage names those whose alliance is loved.
rows.anchor: عقب النهى عن موالاة من تجب معاداتهم ذكر من تحب موالاتهم

words: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular «walī» despite a plural list makes God’s authority foundational and the others’ derivative; a plural would lose that hierarchy.
rows.anchor: الولاية لله أصل ولغيره تبع ولو قيل إنما أولياؤكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be appositional to «those who believe», predicate of an implicit «they are», or an accusative of praise.
rows.anchor: الرفع على البدل من الذين آمنوا أو على هم الذين أو النصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: they give alms while bowing in prayer.
rows.anchor: والواو فى ﴿ وهم راكعون ﴾ للحال أى يؤتونها فى حال ركوعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said the verse came down about ʿAlī when a petitioner asked him as he bowed and he dropped his ring with little movement.
rows.anchor: قيل أنها نزلت فى على رضى الله عنه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع فى صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the plural although the reported occasion involved one person, encouraging others to imitate him and attain like reward.
rows.anchor: وورد بلفظ الجمع و إن كلان السبب فيه واحدا ترغيبا للناس فى مثل فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows charity during prayer is permissible and a small action does not invalidate prayer.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على جواز الصدقة فى الصلاة وعلى أن الفعل القليل لا يفسد الصلاة

words: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To take God, the Messenger, and believers as allies may mean making them protectors or becoming their ally.
rows.anchor: يتخذه وليا أو يكن وليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «God’s party» may replace a pronoun, meaning «they are the victors».
rows.anchor: من إقامة الظاهر مقام الضمير أى فإنهم هم الغالبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God’s party means the Messenger and believers; whoever allies with them joins a force that cannot be overcome.
rows.anchor: أو المراد بحزب الله الرسول والمؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥizb is a group gathered around a matter; its root also describes a matter striking or affecting people.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون الأمر حزبهم أى أصابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come before God for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive alone, without property or helper; furādā is a plural like asīr/asārā.
rows.anchor: منفردين بلا مال ولا معين هو جمع فريد كاسير وأسارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «As We created you» describes their coming in the accusative: they come as they were first created.
rows.anchor: فى محل النصب صفة لمصدر جئتمونا أى مجيئا مثل ما خلقناكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They return alone in the form in which they were born.
rows.anchor: على الهيآت التى ولدتم عليها فى الانفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God bestowed is what He had given them as property; they leave it behind and carry away not even a tiny amount.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وراء ظهوركم ﴾ ولم تحتملوا منه نقيرا

words: شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not see the intercessors they claimed were partners in their worship.
rows.anchor: فى استعبادكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says bayn means connection, though the word also means separation or estrangement; cited poetry evokes longing for separation.
rows.anchor: عن الزجاج والبين الوصل والهجر قال فوالله لولا البين لم يكن الهوى

rows.speaker: مدنى وعلى وحفص
rows.claim: The Medinan reader, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read «baynakum» with fatḥa, meaning that severing occurred among them.
rows.anchor: بينكم مدنى وعلى وحفص أى وقع التقطع بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they claimed disappeared, was wasted, and proved false.
rows.anchor: وضاع وبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation and shaping refer to Adam: God created him as unshaped clay and then shaped him, as the following command to the angels shows.
rows.anchor: أي خلقنا أباكم آدم عليه السلام طينا غير مصور ثم صورناه بعد ذلك دليله

words: إلا إبليس لم يكن من الساجدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs was not among those who prostrated to Adam.
rows.anchor: ممن سجد لآدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what prevented Iblīs from prostrating; «lā» is extra, as in the parallel passages 38:75 and 57:29.
rows.anchor: ولا زائدة بدليل ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is linked to 38:75 and 57:29, where the corresponding «lā» is also treated as extra.
rows.anchor: بدليل ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي ومثلها لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command shows that commands entail obligation; asking about the obstacle despite knowing it rebukes Iblīs and exposes his defiance, disbelief, and pride.
rows.anchor: فيه دليل على أن الأمر للوجوب والسؤال عن المانع من السجود مع علمه به للتوبيخ

words: أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs wrongly claimed superiority: clay has weight, patience, modesty, and endurance, while fire is impulsive, proud, destructive, and treacherous; earth fosters trust and growth.
rows.anchor: وقد أخطأ الخبيث بل الطين أفضل لرزانته ووقاره ومنه الحلم والحياء والصبر

words: خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs was the first to use analogy, but analogy is invalid against an explicit text; his comparison defied the command and relied on a false measure.
rows.anchor: وقول نافى القياس أول من قاس ابليس قياس على أن القياس عند مثبته مردود عند وجود النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than answer directly, Iblīs claimed superiority and its cause, implicitly saying that this supposed superiority stopped him; he deemed a superior prostrating to an inferior irrational.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد استأنف قصة وأخبر فيها عن نفسه بالفضل على آدم عليه السلام وبعلة فضله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addressed Adam after expelling Iblīs from the Garden.
rows.anchor: وقلنا يا آدم بعد إخراج ابليس من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Dwell» means take the Garden as your residence.
rows.anchor: اتخذها مسكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could eat wherever they wished but were forbidden to approach the tree lest they become wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is repeated, quiet, unhurried speech; «waswasa lahu» means whispering for someone, whereas «waswasa ilayhi» means casting it to him.
rows.anchor: وسوس إذا تكلم كلاما خفيا يكرره وهو غير متئد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form for a man is «musawwis» with kasra, not «musawwas» with fatḥa; one says «musawwas lahu» or «musawwas ilayhi» of the recipient.
rows.anchor: ورجل موسوس بكسر الواو ولا يقال موسوس بالفتح

words: ليبدي لهما ما ووري عنهما من سوآتهما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan aimed to expose what was concealed of their nakedness; uncovering private parts has always been repugnant to nature and reason and is a grave matter.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كشف العورة من عظائم الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second wāw is a long vowel, so it is not hamzated; two moving wāws would be heavy, unlike a wāw followed by a silent one.
rows.anchor: لأن الثانية مدة كألف وارى فكما لم يجب همزها فى واعد لم يجب فى وورى

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads «ūrī» with metathesis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أورى بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan claimed they were forbidden the tree lest they become angels who know good and evil and no longer need food.
rows.anchor: إلا كراهة أن تكونا ملكين تعلمان الخير الشر وتستغنيان عن الغذاء

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: A reading has «malikayn», two kings, supported by «an imperishable dominion».
rows.anchor: وقرىء ملكين لقوله وملك لا يبلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The everliving are those who do not die and remain dwelling in the Garden.
rows.anchor: من الذين لا يموتون ويبقون فى الجنة ساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭ means justice and what every rational person recognizes as good, so God cannot command indecency.
rows.anchor: بالعدل وبما هو حسن عند كل عاقل فكيف يأمر بالفحشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may mean to direct yourselves uprightly to God’s worship without turning elsewhere at every prayer time or place of prostration.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد ﴾ وقل أقيموا وجوهكم أى اقصدوا عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Call upon Him» here means worship Him.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وادعوه ﴾ واعبدوه ﴿ مخلصين له الدين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity means obedience done purely while seeking God’s face.
rows.anchor: أى الطاعة مبتغين بها وجهه خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God first created people, He will resurrect them to recompense their deeds; initial creation refutes denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كما بدأكم تعودون ﴾ كما أنشأكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajfa was an earthquake.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأخذتهم الرجفة ﴾ الزلزلة ﴿ فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين ﴾ ميتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were lying dead in their homes.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين ﴾ ميتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first «those who denied Shuʿayb» is the subject whose predicate is «as though they had never lived there»; yaghnu means residing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ الذين كذبوا شعيبا ﴾ مبتدأ خبره ﴿ كأن لم يغنوا فيها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Lam yaghnu» means they had not remained or lived in the land.
rows.anchor: لم يقيموا فيها غنى بالمكان أقام

words: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause restricts the title of losers to Shuʿayb’s deniers: they were destroyed as though never there, while his followers were saved and were the real winners.
rows.anchor: وفى هذا الابتداء معنى الاختصاص كأنه قي الذين كذبوا شعيبا المخصوصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating «those who denied Shuʿayb» magnifies their denial and what befell them.
rows.anchor: مبالغة واستعظام لتكذيهم ولما جرى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed them throughout the earth, so no land was without a group of them.
rows.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها فلا تخلوا بلد من فرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous may be those who believed in Medina or those beyond China.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أمما منهم الصالحون ﴾ الذين آمنوا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those below that standard are people beneath righteousness, namely wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: ومنهم ناس دون ذلك الوصف منحطون عنه وهم الفسقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Dūna dhālik» is nominative as an adjective of an omitted noun: some people below that standard.
rows.anchor: ومحل دون ذلك الرفع وهو صفة لموصوف محذوف أى ومنهم ناس منحطون عن الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and bad things are blessings and afflictions, including abundance and drought.
rows.anchor: بالنعم والنقم والخصب والحدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «So that they may return» means cease wrongdoing and repent.
rows.anchor: ينتهوه فينيبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Those you call» means those you worship and name as gods.
rows.anchor: أى تعبدونهم وتسمونهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are servants like their worshippers: created, owned, and controlled.
rows.anchor: أى مخلقون مملوكون امثالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call on them to bring benefit or avert harm; let them answer if you truly believe they are gods.
rows.anchor: ﴾ لجلب نفع أو دفع ضر ﴿ فليستجيبوا لكم ﴾ فليجيبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions show idols lack the worshippers’ ability to walk, grasp, see, or hear, so it is irrational to worship beings inferior to them.
rows.anchor: الأعراف 185 190 ﴿ أم لهم أيد يبطشون بها ﴾ يتناولون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to summon the idols for aid in opposing him.
rows.anchor: واستعينوا بهم فى عداوتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges the idolaters and their idols to plot against him together.
rows.anchor: جميعا أنتم وشركاؤكم

rows.speaker: يعقوب وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads with yāʾ, and Abū ʿAmr agrees when continuing recitation.
rows.anchor: بالياء يعقوب وافقه أبو عمرو فى الوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «Do not give me respite» means he does not care about them; they had threatened him with their idols, so he was ordered to challenge them.
rows.anchor: فانى لا أبالى بكم وكانوا قد خوفوه ى لهتم فأمر أن يخاطبهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those «with your Lord» are the angels, with Him in rank and station, not physical location.
rows.anchor: مكانة ومنزلة لا مكانا ونزلا يعنى الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not deem themselves too exalted for worship.
rows.anchor: لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ﴾ الأعراف 195 تعظمون عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They glorify God by declaring Him free of what is unbefitting.
rows.anchor: وينزهونه عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reserve prostration and worship for God and associate no one with Him.
rows.anchor: ويختصونه بالعبادة لا يشركون به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heading describes Sūrat al-Anfāl as Medinan and gives its length as five, six, or seventy-seven verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الأنفال مدنية وهى خمس أو ست أو سبع وسبعون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers addressed are Abū Sufyān and his companions.
rows.anchor: أى أبى سفيان وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must stop hostility and fighting against the Messenger by entering Islam.
rows.anchor: عماهم عليه من عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقتلاه بالدخول فى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop, their past hostility will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: لهم من الاعداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they resume fighting, earlier peoples’ destruction and punishment will apply in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: بالإهلاك فى الدنيا والعذاب قفى العقى ب أو معناه

words: إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, stopping means abandoning disbelief and becoming Muslim, in which case prior disbelief and sins are forgiven.
rows.anchor: أن الكفار إذا انتهوع عن الكفر وأسلموا غفرلهم ماقد سلف

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa cites this verse to argue that an apostate who returns to Islam need not make up worship missed while apostate.
rows.anchor: وبه احتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله فى أن المرتد إذا أسلم لم يلزمه قضاء العبادات المتروكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source counts three hundred hypocritical men and one hundred seventy hypocritical women.
rows.anchor: الرجال المنافقون كانوا ثلثمائة والنساء المنافقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are like one self; this denies that they belong to believers and refutes their claim «we are of you», reinforcing «they are not of you».
rows.anchor: وفيه نفى أن يكونوا من المؤمنين وتكذيبهم فى قولهم ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وتقرير لقوله وما هم منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They command unbelief and disobedience and forbid obedience and faith, opposite to believers.
rows.anchor: بالكفر والعصيان ﴿ وينهون عن المعروف ﴾ عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withhold out of stinginess alms and spending in God’s path.
rows.anchor: شحا بالمبار والصدقات والإنفاق فى سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «They forgot God» may mean abandoning His command or neglecting His remembrance.
rows.anchor: تركوا امره أو غفلوا ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgetting them means leaving them without mercy and favor.
rows.anchor: فتركهم من رحمته وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are fully rebellious in unbelief and stripped of every good; Muslims should avoid earning this harsh label.
rows.anchor: هم الكاملون فى الفسق الذي هو التمرد فى الكفر والانسلاخ عن كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing men and women are allies through mutual support and compassion.
rows.anchor: فى التناصر والتراحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They command obedience and faith and forbid idolatry and disobedience.
rows.anchor: بالطاعة و الإيمان ﴿ وينهون عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future marker guarantees the promised mercy, just as future wording can emphasize a threat.
rows.anchor: السين مفيدة وجود الرحمة لا محالة فهى تؤكد الوعد كما تؤكد الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and able to grant reward or impose punishment.
rows.anchor: عزيز ﴾ غالب على كل شيء قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise, placing everything in its proper place.
rows.anchor: واضع كل موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave them wealth and they attained what they wished for.
rows.anchor: أعطاهم الله المال ونالوا مناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withheld God’s due and did not fulfill their covenant.
rows.anchor: منعوا حق الله ولم يفوا بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned from obedience to God and persisted in their aversion.
rows.anchor: عن طاعة الله ﴿ وهم معرضون ﴾ مصرون على الاعراض
